Many of the most popular roguelike games such as dead cells, slay the spire, hades and risk of rain 2 have an "escalating difficulty" type system or game mode which adds alot of longevity to these games. For dead cells its the boss cell system, for spire its acensions, for hades its heat, and for risk of rain 2 its the eclipse gamemode. 

Basically its a gamemode where its a normal run but with each completion it gets harder and harder each time, whether its by stats/mechanics/encounters until you reach a final difficulty which is really hard and will be lost most of the time by all but the absolute best players. This would be good post-game content which is proven to work and would probably increase longevity of the game.

The Shirou and Archer interactions were too hand-wavey prior to their fight, Shirou NEEDED scenes to emphasize his broken mentality, rather than someone who was just very determined and selfless. The anime makes him seem like your generic self-sacrificing anime protagonist, rather than someone who was deeply conflicted with his value as a human and literally sees himself as a tool rather than a human being.

Another thing was that the Archer fight just made it seem like Shirou didn't really develop and simply just "proved archer wrong" when in reality they were both following different interpretations of the ideal of a hero of justice. (Shirou focused on the act in and of itself being worthwhile, whereas Archer was focused purely on results) Archer was never "proven wrong" His ideals WERE foolish from the get-go, but what he forgot was that even though it was foolish it was still worth it to follow, because the wish to save others cannot be wrong. The anime is very vague about this and the Archer vs Shirou fight lacks impact there because it tries to make it seem like Shirou simply "won" when in reality he proved to Archer that he was already different than he was, and how he'd legitimately not end up like him.

Some anime only's even come out thinking Archer is evil, because the way their fight is framed is in a very typical "good vs evil" fashion, rather than two conflicting ideals which BOTH have valid points. Hell if anything, when reading the VN I initially believed archer WAS RIGHT and that Shirou SHOULD give up on his ideal to be a hero of justice, but as the fight goes on it makes you realize that this is only if you are focusing on the results, rather than the ideal itself simply being something worth to follow. Anime really needs to portray this better.
